_about: Hand check and failure labels for the first official S3 run, written after reading every reply and before any fix (CRITERIA.md). 'hand' is the hand verdict where it differs from the marker; the marker's score stays the official one. Labels: retrieval, wrong item retrieved, wrong item used, prompt/formatting, scorer, model behaviour.

S1-05.why: Opens with 'I don't have that in your memory', then gives the note. Telling the user it isn't saved when it is counts as wrong.

S1-25.why: Same: says 'I don't have that' and then gives the milk price.

S1-12.why: Asked only when the LIC premium is due; the date is right. The task rule also requires the amount, which the question did not ask for (task rule too strict).

S1-37.why: Code-built answer quotes the original sentence (18 December) but states 'Now: on Monday 21 December 2026'. Correct and clear, though the old date appears in the quote.

S1-06.why: Team call put at 10 am (it is 11 am), lists the night shift that starts on 14 December, and invents an 'Amma's birthday celebration'. The marker only checked that 11:00 appears and the order.

S1-25.why: Says 'I don't have that' and then gives the milk price.

S1-12.why: As in run (b): the date asked for is right; the rule also wants the amount.

S1-18.why: Plain Qwen says it has no access; it passes only because the word 'paid' appears in 'check if your water bill is paid'.

marker_errors_seen: A month name followed by a numbered list item ('15 December.\n2. Pay') is read as a date (2 December). In run (b) this made the guard reject a correct first answer on S1-27, which then fell back to a code-built answer. In run (a) it adds a false invented date (5/1) to S1-23, which fails for other reasons anyway.
Listing the empty days of the asked week ('Tuesday 15 December: No appointments') counts as invented dates. This sent S1-47 in run (b) to a code-built answer.
